Page 01chapter 0 · page 1

KEYPAD MATRIX SCAN. Strobes the key-column lines (R1..R5) one at a time and reads the row lines (K1..K4) with KNEZ/TKA. On a hit it saves the column (M(0,14)), debounces, reads the row (M(0,15)), and waits for release. The pressed key = (column, row). The K bus is shared: a column strobe selects keypad rows, R6 selects the DIN inputs, R11 selects the SRAM data.

Page 05chapter 0 · page 5

Halted-mode command handling (part of the PGM command path; partially traced). A subroutine here (RETN at 05:15) drives output lines R14/R15 from flag bits in M(4,d); from 05:16 it tests state bits in file 4 and branches to several command-handler pages (1/6/7/8/b/d at :02) -- the routing that sends a PGM digit to its handler. Exact per-command mapping still being traced.

7-SEGMENT DISPLAY REFRESH. Multiplexes the six digits: for each, TDO drives the segments (the hardware OPLA decodes the nibble to a 7-seg pattern) and SETR strobes that digit's common line (R0..R5); a short delay holds it lit, then RSTR moves to the next. SL into TDO = the decimal point (CARRY / ZERO / 1Hz flag dots).

Page 28chapter 2 · page 8

1Hz CLOCK ADVANCE = background timekeeping (found by emulation). Called from the main dispatcher on each NEW 1Hz pulse (the 1Hz signal output must be wired to DIN 4). Advances the BCD software clock in file 4: M(4,0)=sec-units M(4,1)=sec-tens M(4,2)=min-units M(4,3)=min-tens M(4,4)=hr-units M(4,5)=hr-tens, with cascading carry (IMAC+TAM per digit; roll sec1 at 10 via ACxAC 5, sec10 at 6 = 60s via ACxAC 9, etc.). 28:01 SBIT 3 on M(4,6) is the "this pulse already counted" edge-detect latch (so it advances once per pulse, not while DIN4 stays high). This is the same file-4 clock the F06 TIME handler (12:18) copies into RA..RF, and that PGM 3/4 set/show. Verified: toggle DIN4 in dev-support/microtronic_emu.py -> M(4,0) ticks and carries at 10s/60s.

Page 30chapter 3 · page 0

PGM 5 (CLEAR-RAM) + PGM 6 (LOAD-NOP) shared handler (VERIFIED by emulation). An ACxAC command sub-dispatch (30:00-0e) selects the fill VALUE, then a shared loop blanks the whole program store: setup at 30:13 seeds the SRAM address pointer M(1,5):M(1,4)=FF, then 30:1f-30 walks that 8-bit address down to 0, writing the fill value into each slot via the SRAM writer at 0c:02 (called from 30:29, returning to 30:2a), until the address wraps. PGM 6 writes F01 (NOP); PGM 5 writes 000. Both confirmed by running the ROM (press PGM then 6/5 -> all 256 slots become F01/000). dev-support/microtronic_emu.py.

Page 3achapter 3 · page a

PGM 7 = the NIM GAME (Busch manual p.7-8) -- the one built-in stored as Microtronic CODE, not native TMS. Each instruction = three TCMIY constants (its three hex digits, stored LOW-NIBBLE-FIRST); a CALL to the loader at 3a:00 writes it into external SRAM, and the interpreter then runs it like any typed-in program. ~66-69 instructions across 3a-3f, identified by Decle/Jason (Jason published a full disassembly). The other PGM 0-6 are native TMS routines elsewhere: 0 self-test, 1/2 cassette load/save, 3/4 set/show time, 5 clear RAM, 6 load-NOP.
3a:0042TCY4program loader: write the just-built 3-nibble instruction to the next SRAM slot and advance the address
3a:013eIMACbump the SRAM write pointer (increment; carry into the high nibble)
